To convert **io2** volumes created before November 21, 2023, to **io2** Block Express volumes, [modify the IOPS or size of the volume](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-modify-volume.html).\\n\\n**Important:** If you created your **io1** volume before December 6, 2017, then you must upgrade the volume to io2 Block Express. Other instance\\n types can be attached to volumes provisioned with up to 64,000 IOPS, but can achieve up to 32,000\\n IOPS\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/provisioned-iops.html\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Class: Aws::EC2::Types::CreateVolumeRequest\\n \\n \u2014 AWS SDK for Ruby V2\",\"context\":\"### #**iops** \u21d2 Integer\\n\\nThe number of I/O operations per second (IOPS) to provision for an `io1`\\nor `io2` volume, with a maximum ratio of 50 IOPS/GiB for `io1`, and 500\\nIOPS/GiB for `io2`. Range is 100 to 64,000 IOPS for volumes in most\\nRegions. Maximum IOPS of 64,000 is guaranteed only on Nitro-based\\ninstances. Other instance families guarantee performance up to\\n32,000 IOPS. For more information, see Amazon EBS volume types in\\nthe *Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud User Guide*.\\n\\nThis parameter is valid only for Provisioned IOPS SSD (`io1` and `io2`)\\nvolumes.\\n\\nReturns:\\n\\n* (Integer)\\n \u2014\\n\\n The number of I/O operations per second (IOPS) to provision for an `io1` or `io2` volume, with a maximum ratio of 50 IOPS/GiB for `io1`, and 500 IOPS/GiB for `io2`\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-ruby/v2/api/Aws/EC2/Types/CreateVolumeRequest.html\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Look up EBS io2 IOPS quota documentation"}

{"id": "ea39ef3e-639b-41de-88bb-41d70d9cfc81", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "You've hit the regional quota for total provisioned io2 IOPS. It's an account-level limit, not a limit on one volume. The default is 100,000 IOPS per Region, and it counts the IOPS of all your existing io2 volumes. If you already have io2 volumes in that Region, the new 150K request is added to their total.

**What to do**

1. **Request a quota increase.** In Service Quotas, go to Amazon EBS and find **IOPS for Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) volumes**. Request a value that covers your existing io2 IOPS plus the 150K for the new volume. Make sure you're in the Region where you're creating the volume, because quotas are per Region. A CLI example:
   ```
   aws service-quotas list-service-quotas --service-code ebs --region <region> \
     --query "Quotas[?contains(QuotaName,'io2')]"
   aws service-quotas request-service-quota-increase --service-code ebs \
     --quota-code <code-from-above> --desired-value 300000 --region <region>
   ```
   Small increases are often approved automatically. Larger ones may need AWS Support review, which can take a while. If the request stalls, open a Support case.

2. **Check how much io2 IOPS is already in use.** Other io2 volumes, including unattached ones, count toward the quota. Unused volumes or over-provisioned IOPS can free up room. You can lower IOPS on an existing volume with `modify-volume`.

3. **Check that 150K is achievable for your setup.**
   - A single io2 volume can provision up to 256,000 IOPS, but only at 500 IOPS/GiB or less. 150K IOPS needs a volume of at least 300 GiB.
   - To get more than 64,000 IOPS, the volume must be attached to a **Nitro-based instance**. Other instance types are limited to 64,000 provisioned IOPS and get about 32,000 in practice.
   - If one instance can't drive 150K, you can stripe several volumes with RAID 0. That also helps you stay within per-volume limits.

4. **Work around it while you wait.** You can create the volume with fewer IOPS now, up to the headroom you have left under the quota. After the quota is raised, increase the IOPS with `modify-volume`, which works while the volume is in use.

I can check your current io2 quota and usage in a specific Region if you tell me which one and which account.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
